- **status:** PARTIAL. The code and unit tests are done. W2-96's formal accept fails on S-D10a (3 cases), and W2-92's map is now refused.
- **work_completed:**
  - **F1, the reader:** after the first line name, the reader scans the whole rest of the cell, notes included. Names inside backticks (test or file names) are skipped.
    - A further line name is **read**, with any list it starts, when a join comes just before it: `,` `;` `/` `&` `+` `(` `and` `or` `with`.
    - A name that only repeats a line already read is ignored, e.g. `KPI 1 (S1; …)`.
    - **Any other further line name refuses the cell** with `ACCEPT_MAP_UNREADABLE`, as before. That covers `item F2`, `F1's fixture`, `[I4 F14]`, `[F14]` and `S1 then S2`.
    - Square brackets do not count as a join: in maps they are citations, often a review's finding.
    - New forms read: `S2-S4`, `Success 2–Success 4` (a range across kinds is refused) and `Success 1 to 3` (not `… to 3 cases`, which is a count). `or` is now a join.
    - A possessive with no space (`W2-61's 20-question`) no longer reads as success-20.
    - All of the brief's forms are read: W1-49 rows 88 and 89, W2-92's `Success 6 with success 4.`, `(and failure 2)`, `— and failure 2`, `failures 4, 5`.
  - **Scope (b):**
    - `optin` only ever holds `breadth`. When the map's cases need `lifted`, the result has `"report_only": ["lifted"]`.
    - A small pytest plugin, written into the run's private folder and removed with it, records which cases the `lifted` list left out, by file and name only.
    - A line that ran no case and whose every item names a left-out case gets `"outcome": "report-only"` and `"note": "report-only (lifted)"`. Text output is the same JSON, so it shows that string too.
    - Left-out cases do not fail a line as "named test not found", so a line with cases in `lifted` and elsewhere is measured on the cases that ran.
    - A line that runs zero for any other reason still fails.
    - **My own choice:** a run in which every line is report-only fails, because it measures nothing.
  - **F3:** once the groups are set, every error result carries `optin` and `report_only`, including a crash inside the run or the report.

- **discoveries:**
  - **W2-92 row 128 is refused** because of `S1's record route`. I treat a possessive (`X's`) mention as a reference rather than a listing, the same rule that refuses W2-77's `F1's fixture`. This needs a map fix row (not mine): either `Success 6, success 4 and success 1` or drop the S1 mention.
  - **S-D10a's 3 reds** probably come from the designer's variants that assume `lifted` is enabled (`a-case-in-lifted-passes`, `lines-in-both-groups-through-every-list-name`). The round-1 review said scope (b) needs those rewritten. I have not confirmed this, because I don't read the tests.
- **risks:**
  - Reading a line named after `(` or `with` could map a case to a line it only cross-references, as in W2-72's F headings. That only adds cases to that line.
  - Report-only relies on pytest's deselect hook. A list that leaves cases out some other way would make those lines fail, never pass.
  - The first `gov accept` ran on commit `dac10e5df`; the later four may have loaded the `[` edit, which I made while they ran. The comparison shows that edit changes no map's reading, so the results are unaffected.
- **lessons:** In map prose, F-numbers are often review findings (`[I4 F14]`, `item F2`, `F1's`), so "read everything" is not safe; only a join before a name marks a listing.
